H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper describes a flat sequential PLC workflow with level states, auto up/down actions, manual buttons, and emergency stop; it does not define parent states or nested sub-FSMs.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Multiple guarded transitions are present: water-level ranges 0-14 cm, 14-19 cm, 19-25 cm; AUTO UP after level 3; AUTO DOWN after level 1; hoist stop on upper/lower limit switch.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: State-dependent outputs are central: green/yellow/red tower lights, red-level buzzer, motor hoist ON for opening/closing, and motor OFF at limit switches, with outputs held while level conditions remain true.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The emergency switch is a system-level stop: the paper says it is used to stop system operation OFF in dangerous or fault situations and black-box test 11 turns the control system off by pressing it.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: The core state, guard, and action behavior is concentrated in the Flowchart Kerja Alat subsection and then repeated in black-box tests; no state requires non-adjacent reconstruction.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as Emergency Switch, Manual Up/Down, and limit switch are accompanied by explicit behavior descriptions, so no extra domain rule must be inferred.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Although written as prose, each level/action mapping is stated near the corresponding level condition in the flowchart narrative.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The modeled transition logic combines level condition with operator button events and limit-switch stopping conditions, e.g. level 3 plus AUTO UP, then run until a limit switch is activated.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No composite parent state or parent-level entry/during/exit behavior is described.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: Emergency Switch is described as stopping the whole control system, a cross-cutting escape that would apply regardless of the current level or hoist movement state.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: No composite-state initialization or pseudo-state chain appears.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: There are several simple threshold and boolean guards over water level, operator buttons, and limit switches, but no deep arithmetic guard network.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: The emergency stop applies globally to the level and movement states, so a forced transition can encode one rule instead of duplicating it across many states.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Outputs are concrete hardware effects: tower lights, buzzer, pilot lamp, and mini-hoist motor commands.

one_line_pitch: A flat but action-heavy PLC dam-gate sequence stresses guard extraction, output attribution, and global emergency-stop encoding more than hierarchical reconstruction.
rationale: This is a meaningful stress-test sample because the paper gives a concrete semi-automatic PLC sequence with water-level guards, operator-triggered transitions, hoist limit stops, continuous indicator outputs, and a system-wide emergency stop. Its main weakness as a top candidate is the absence of hierarchical or composite-state structure, so it primarily stresses guards, actions, and global escape behavior rather than the full Apvrille-style hierarchy/action/guard failure surface.
